sources.title: Enhanced A2A Protect
sources.supports: A2A deployment, opt-in signals and reported detection lift

financial_anchor.caveat: Reported scale proxy; litigation and mix affect normalization

ai_claim.claim: Visa deploys network-level ML risk scores in issuer authorization and A2A fraud workflows; an identified issuer reports prevented fraud and Visa reports a 75% A2A detection increase.
ai_claim.scope: Selected risk products and customers, not all Visa transactions
ai_claim.limitation: No disclosed matched protocol, sample, price, implementation cost or retained-cash bridge

strongest_counterevidence.claim: Comparable network/bank models, client incentives and alternative rails can replicate or absorb the gain; Q3 client incentives rose 18% against 14% revenue growth.
strongest_counterevidence.limitation: One quarter does not identify structural pass-through or AI causality

rights_limit: Participants originate much of the data. Public material proves scoring and opt-in A2A sharing, not unrestricted pooled training or cross-customer reuse rights.
materiality_summary: The 5% screen equals $1.200bn on FY2025 reported operating profit. Available product metrics do not establish retained Visa contribution of that size.
g2_provisional: Limited pass: E2 production evidence and a measurable KPI path exist, but controlled quality-adjusted evidence and material cash capture are absent.
unresolved_questions: What paid volume and renewal attach to each risk product?
What are customer-specific versus pooled-learning rights?
Do matched cohorts improve fraud and false declines after total cost?
